steps.content:
Over the years, the Black Rings have become a unit we use to measure time: N.F. 89, BR-001. N.F. 104, BR-002. N.F. 112, BR-004... But before them, there was another way to define an era.
In N.F. 68, she kindled the first light amid the ruins. In N.F. 72, she saved more than twenty thousand lives. In N.F. 76, Mania detection technology was born...
Today, countless barriers shield us from Mania. Yet this unsung hero spent her entire life reminding us that, in the face of disaster, humanity's final line of defense has always been our resolve to stand by one another.
This is not the story of a single hero. It is the story of humanity itself.
This film is dedicated to every brave soul who walks through the ashes.
— Maris Andre

As the text on the screen fades away, thunderous applause fills the elegant, ornate memorial hall. The chandelier gradually lights up as the guests raise their glasses in unison, their expressions sincere, some even teary-eyed.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: Let us raise a toast to the subject of our documentary, Ms. Maris Andre, and to every unsung hero among us.

The young aristocrat raises his glass to the guests. Ever since inheriting the family enterprise a year ago, he has abandoned the family's traditionally low-profile approach, using the media to showcase its collection to the public. He has also been doing everything he can to secure a place in the city's high society.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I'd like to take a look at the calligraphy and paintings over there. Shall we, Chief?
Her calm, gentle voice remains unperturbed by the excitement buzzing around her. Celine loops her arm through yours and leads you toward the exhibits that caught her eye.

The Pierce villa is vast. After winding your way through its endless corridors, you arrive at the memorial hall just as the opening ceremony draws to a close. The guests disperse like a school of well-fed fish, each drifting at their own pace through the currents of history, admiring the grand portrait of Ms. Maris behind low-reflection glass with solemn reverence.

steps.speaker: Curator
steps.content: The layout and arrangement of the memorial hall are truly well thought out. It chronicles Ms. Maris's life while painting a vivid picture of the Disians' everyday life at the time. Ms. Maris was truly the symbol of that era...

steps.speaker: Pseudo-historian
steps.content: Indeed. She witnessed DisCity's growth from its infancy, through its roaring golden age, into the global powerhouse it is today...

steps.speaker: Painter
steps.content: General Augustus is immortalized by Breaching BR-005. Likewise, Ms. Maris deserves a painting of her own, Silent Night Walk. The painting on that wall is my tribute to her. I never had the chance to meet her in person, but in my heart, she is a goddess bearing a lantern, lighting the way for a world ravaged by Mania.

steps.speaker: Writer
steps.content: "Ms. Andre's gaze was ever piercing, always insightful. There burned within her eyes an indestructible flame." A line from the biography Maris of Glorie. What a masterpiece! If you look closely at the painting, you can actually see the light of her lantern reflected in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: Oh, that reminds me. Where is Professor Morton?

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: Ladies and gentlemen! You are all distinguished figures in your respective fields, and dear friends who share my passion. So allow me to speak from the heart...
The hall buzzes with voices, but these individuals stand out in particular, speaking loudly and confidently.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm afraid these people all play a part in fabricating the image of Maris Andre. That painting doesn't even show her full face. Are they afraid of getting caught using a real person's face as reference?

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: They kept the face blurry because they were not trying to make a portrait of a real person, but a "symbol of an era."

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: The painter creates the image, the writer shapes the persona, the media stirs public empathy, and the curator pieces together these fabricated fragments into a coherent narrative. That is all it takes to make a hero. Human beings have always been good at creating idols.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: It's a shame that the only genuine antique in this entire hall is that crystal chandelier. Everything else is a forgery. It seems Mr. Pierce has just enough sense to know that the real treasures are best kept hidden.

The crowd suddenly parts. Pierce approaches, champagne glass in hand. As he draws closer, you can clearly see that huge ring on his thumb, a striking piece fashioned in the shape of a three-sided shield.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: Are you... Chief ${PlayerName}? It really is you! I thought I had the wrong person from across the room. And you are...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Nice to meet you, Mr. Pierce. This is the Bureau's archivist.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: A pleasure to meet you! There were so many guests at the peace banquet last time that I never had the chance to speak with you. I hear the MBCC keeps you quite busy... Are you here because you're interested in Ms. Maris's life, or is there some other matter you wish to discuss?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We've been archiving some old files lately, and many of them are from unidentified periods. I heard the memorial hall would be exhibiting materials from the Independence era, so I thought I'd come take a look ahead of time. Please don't feel the need to make any special arrangements for me.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Though I must say, the exhibition downstairs seems rather sparse. I've already taken a full tour and seen most of what's on display.
This is a script you and Celine worked out in advance. Given the Pierce family's eagerness to mingle with the upper echelons, you can easily get his attention this way.

Fortunately for you, Celine rarely appears in public, so she isn't easily recognized. With nothing more than a change of clothes, she can pass herself off as your assistant. After all, if her identity were exposed here, it would be no different from announcing your true purpose out loud.

steps.speaker: Editor-in-Chief
steps.content: Get the cameraman over here! This could be tomorrow's headline.

steps.speaker: Pseudo-historian
steps.content: I seem to recall the Chief's dance partner last time was that rather imposing general. But it's not the same person this time...

A crowd begins to gather. Pierce's smile deepens. He waves a server over, murmurs a few words, then turns and gestures for you, one of DisCity's most talked-about public figures these days, to join him.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: What matters to society matters to me. As witnesses to DisCity's history, the Pierce family has always valued its bonds with those who seek the truth.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: Indeed, there are some limitations as to what we can display downstairs. If you'd like to see some rarer exhibits, Chief, please follow me.
Pierce leads you both upstairs courteously. You spend nearly ten minutes navigating the labyrinthine corridors before he finally stops before a pair of heavy redwood doors.

It is a lavish study, its decor appearing as though it had been salvaged from some grand old building and carefully reassembled here. Books and folders line the shelves in neat rows. Though the origins of the antique furnishings are unknown, they all appear exceedingly luxurious.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: You're looking at my family's private collection, Chief. Though we're still in the same building as the memorial hall, this area is subject to much stricter security measures, as it houses a far more important collection.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: This area is equipped with the finest climate control systems, allowing us to safely incorporate these artifacts into our daily lives. Any single piece you see in this room could easily become the centerpiece of an exhibition at any public museum.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A collection of this size must have taken considerable money and effort to maintain.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: Haha, naturally. Three generations of my family's dedication are preserved in this room. Quite a few pieces were acquired through... special means. You'll never see such pieces on the open market. My ancestors were content simply to collect, but I believe these treasures deserve to be admired by more people.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: Is there any particular piece that catches your eye, Chief? I'd be happy to give you a proper introduction.

Wine is served, and you settle into the seat across from Pierce for a rather diplomatic conversation. Celine wanders around the room before stopping at the shelves, and within moments, she is completely absorbed. Judging by her reaction, she must have taken an interest in a few items from the collection.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Mr. Pierce, please excuse my assistant. She works best without an audience, so kindly let her be. Now, do tell me more about your family. That ring on your thumb has caught my attention.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: Heh, you have a keen eye, Chief. It bears my family's crest and motto, passed down for over a century. The three shields symbolize collection, scholarship, and legacy...

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: And this motto is an old saying that predates Nightfall, meaning "Faithful to Memory." It reflects the way my family has always approached history...

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: And wouldn't it be ironic if the Pierces turned out to be fabricators of history?
Celine's voice comes from behind. She strides over, cradling an open book which belongs to the collection here. When she stops in front of you both, a cold glint flashes in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Desertification along DisCity's borders is severe, so livestock are a scarce resource. Most books there are made from a local plant fiber renowned for its exceptional strength. You can imagine how difficult it would be to find a notebook bound with leather cord in a satellite town.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: After DisCity's mining districts fell into decline, Syndican literature entered a golden age. Memories of Grace River was never intended as an elegy for the DisCorps. Just because Grace River later became known as the Rust—and rust is associated with metal—doesn't make the book a legacy of the Shattered Blade.
Celine flips through the pages with increasing speed. Pierce grows visibly restless, his eyes darting to you questioningly. You spread your hands and feign innocence.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Chief, with such unreliable sources, I'm afraid it's impossible to establish a timeline for our cases that are undeniably real.

By now, even a fool can tell that you are not here for a friendly conversation. Pierce's smile has turned rigid. He stops a passing server, rises from his seat, pours himself a glass from the tray, and makes his way toward Celine.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: I've long heard that the MBCC is home to many talented individuals, but today is the first time I've had the pleasure of meeting one. How long have you worked in the archives, Miss? If you hadn't spotted those flaws, I might never have realized these were forgeries. The Pierce Museum could certainly use someone of your caliber.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: And of course, I would offer something in return for taking your capable assistant off your hands, Chief. I'm aware that certain parties aren't exactly fond of you or the MBCC, and I happen to have some insight into the forces behind them... I know you prefer to confront your opponents openly, but having a better understanding of them is never a disadvantage.
Celine looks almost amused. She pretends to consider the offer seriously before beginning to haggle with you.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: What do you think, Chief? I never imagined my expertise would lead to so many career opportunities. My current research doesn't require much funding, but... surely the Bureau could use a few more comfortable chairs?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If all you want are new chairs, there's no need to switch jobs. I can splurge what's left of this year's budget on furnishing the archives.
Nightingale isn't here anyway. No one can stop you from making empty promises.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Then... what about the offer that gentleman just made? One more friend in the shadows is better than one more enemy in the light, wouldn't you say?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'd much prefer friends in the light, though. The shadows make it difficult to tell friend from foe, and the last thing I want is to hurt an ally by mistake.
She picks up her glass, pours the wine into your empty one, then raises her now-empty glass in a toast toward Pierce.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: What a shame, Mr. Pierce. Granted, I do have the patience to sift through your mountain of mostly forged documents to find the few genuine records, but your current offer simply isn't tempting enough to make me give up my comfortable chair at the Bureau.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: My apologies. I'm afraid I can't raise a glass with you today.
A vein throbs on Pierce's forehead. He deliberates for a moment, then seems to make up his mind. Turning away, he retrieves a glass case kept safe behind layers of tempered glass.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: Given the Chief's generosity toward the Bureau's employees, it's only natural that you would be reluctant to give up your current position, Miss. How about this...

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: These are authentic records from the early Black Ring operations. They contain experimental logs and research data on Mania patients from that era. These documents are priceless materials that have never been revealed to the public.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: With your expertise, I have no doubt you could craft a research report that would shake the entire academic world. And of course, you would receive full credit for it.
Not only is this the original document behind Morton's incomplete copy, but it also contains previously unpublished materials found nowhere else. This is truly an invaluable discovery.
Then again, neither you nor Celine are ordinary people. Pierce's bribe would certainly have no...

You glance over at Celine, only to find her eyes practically glowing as she stares at the documents in Pierce's hands. She looks exactly like a child who has just spotted a lollipop, practically drooling.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Ahem!
Your cough brings Celine back to her senses. She tears her gaze away, though not before stealing several longing glances back at the documents.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Mm... Ahem... That does seem like an irresistible offer. What do you think, Chief?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I believe Mr. Pierce has proven his sincerity. Perhaps you should just accept it.
The moment Celine takes the glass case, an urgent call comes through. Pierce's expression changes.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: What... the Public Security Bureau? An inspector... are you sure?
He wheels around to face you both, the fawning look in his eyes gone, replaced by flustered anger.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: Chief, I know I'm just a nobody compared to someone as important as you, but I came to you in good faith. And this is how you repay me? By sending people to sabotage my exhibition?!
Celine tilts her head ever so slightly, her gaze settling on the hand he's pressing over the box, as though she's spotted something interesting.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: I see... Mr. Pierce, you accuse us of sabotaging your exhibition.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: But you know full well those exhibits downstairs are embarrassingly flawed, and yet you've still chosen to display them. You can see that the face in that painting has been deliberately obscured, and yet you still call it "the symbol of an era."

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Sabotage? Is it even worth the effort? It seems to me your project is already coming apart on its own.
Pierce's expression darkens, but Celine gives him no chance to respond. Her gaze drifts back down to the glass case he's clutching.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: That said, unlike everything downstairs, what you have in your hands is genuine. At least for now, it is still priceless.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: When you took it out just now, I noticed the ink along the edges. Given the temperature and humidity in this room, I'd estimate you have about a year before the ink begins to bleed.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Wild papyrus has long gone extinct. I know of a company capable of developing a substitute fiber, but... for certain historical reasons, they would never be willing to work with a family that has betrayed the motto "Faithful to Memory."

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Is that why you seemed so desperate? You're in such a hurry to find its next owner before it becomes a worthless stack of paper. That's the real reason you were so eager to receive Chief today.
She has barely finished her sentence when an alarm goes off. You can faintly hear the guests' shocked cries and frantic footsteps downstairs.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: What do you want exactly?!
Celine does not answer right away. She simply raises her hand, and every sheet of paper in the room seems to tremble simultaneously.

These pages have rested quietly in this elegant collection room, their deterioration slowed to a near standstill by carefully controlled temperature and humidity. Having been spared the devastation of war and the ordeal of concealment under harsh conditions, many of the documents remain in remarkably good condition.
And yet now they tremble in unison, as though straining against their cage in search of a new guardian.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Many of the manuscripts in your collection were painstakingly crafted by people I knew personally. Your ancestors left them buried in dust for years, and now they are being unearthed only to support a deceptive scheme.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Whether you like it or not, I will return them to the descendants of their authors. I suppose I should thank your family for leaving you with at least a modicum of dignity.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: I see... I see. You've been conspiring together, trying to silence the truth about Maris! That is what this is really about. I won't let you get away with this. I swear...
Finally realizing his opponent's true goal, Pierce lets his anger get the better of him and lunges straight at you.
Even without any help from the Sinners, you think you can handle this pampered brat on your own just fine.
Thump!
A dull, numbing pain shoots through your fist. Pierce lets out a sharp cry, clutches his face in agony, and crumples to the floor with a miserable wail.
The sound of their employer taking a beating reaches the security team outside. They storm in and move to pin you both to the ground.
(Gunshots, smoke)

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: MBCC! Get on the ground and do not resist! You are under arrest!

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, are you alright? My apologies. The Public Security Bureau's operation was compromised, so we were delayed.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm fine. Your timing couldn't have been better. Don't let Pierce get away!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Where's Celine?!

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Cough, cough... I'm... cough... here.
The smoke clears just enough to reveal Celine, eyes red and face smudged from the tear gas. She's clutching the glass case to her chest. The same one Pierce nearly smashed moments ago.

steps.speaker: Celine
steps.content: Tell everyone to be careful! Cough... Every piece in here is precious. Even the fake ones! Oh no, no, no... No more tear gas. Or at least don't aim it at the collection. It will corrode the items!

Dazzling lights still shine in the villa well into the night, though the guests have long since fled. The grand portrait of Maris Andre still watches over the disordered banquet hall in silence. Her face, deliberately obscured behind a veil of mist by the artist, now seems to carry a trace of mockery.

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: Stop, stop! Do you have any idea who you're dealing with?!

steps.speaker: Pierce
steps.content: I am the head of the Pierce family! Just let me explain... This is all a misunderstanding!

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, we've got the guest list from the reception. The Public Security Bureau's media department will handle the follow-up interrogations. Professor Celine's arm was injured by broken glass. She's been taken to the hospital.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Good work. What will we do with the documents and antiques found here?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The Public Security Bureau is conducting a thorough investigation. Under a special requisition order from the library, the entire collection in the Pierce estate, including the potential forgeries, will first be transferred to the Central Library in Paradeisos.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Everything?
As if she's already expecting your surprise, Nightingale gives a small nod of confirmation.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Yes, Chief. Everything.
